subject: Urgent: Clear8Health throughput suppression after policy rollout
messages:

Subject: Sudden drop in throughput / rising errors since Wednesday

Sofia —

We started seeing a sharp increase in failed requests and latency for our account around 06:30 PST on Wednesday (2026-11-18). The error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~8% and p50 latency doubled. We’re seeing a mix of 429s and transient 503s. This is impacting nightly report jobs and some live inference.

Attached are a sample of request IDs and a small log slice (clear8_error_samples.log). Important: this started after the platform team applied the “safety valve” capacity policy you announced last week. Can you confirm if Clear8 has been put on any temporary caps or new policy rules?

We need an acknowledgement and ETA; the ops lead here (Samir) is on this thread. If we can get a rollback or immediate mitigation, that would help us avoid a rollback on our side.

Thanks —
Jill
Director of Platform Ops
Clear8 Health

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jill Porter <jill.porter@clear8health.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden drop in throughput / rising errors since Wednesday

Jill / Sofia —

TL;DR: We’ve identified a policy regression in the safety valve config that caused Clear8’s dedicated tenant to be placed into a conservative throughput limiter. This mistaken mapping reduces burst allowance and forces early request suppression under sustained bursts — leading to the 429s observed.

What we saw:
- Around 06:26 PST the new global policy rollout (policy v2026-11-18.3) applied a QoS mapping rule that matches by organization tag.
- For dedicated tenants we accidentally evaluate token-cost using a per-second rate (tokens/sec) but then apply the window in units of minutes due to a unit conversion bug. The net effect: burst budget is consumed 60x faster than intended for jobs that send short-lived bursts, so the safety valve closes prematurely.
- The policy diff (attached: policy-diff.patch) highlights the bad unit conversion and the extra min-window clamp.

Immediate mitigations in flight (I’ve pushed these 10:00–10:20):
1) Temporarily increased Clear8’s tenant cap to 3x baseline from the console (manual override) — this restores throughput while we produce a patch.
2) Rotated policy to exempt "dedicated" tag from the new window clamp (hotfix rolled by infra team).
3) Enabled fallback routing to the compatible model variant (rwd-base-1-compat) for heavy jobs to reduce token cost while preserving latency.

Impact and ETA:
- Most customer traffic saw errors drop within 12 minutes of the cap increase (we’re at ~0.9% error now from peak ~8%).
- Hotfix rolling to all control-plane nodes now; full rollout ETA 45 minutes.

Next steps:
- Patch the unit-conversion bug and add unit tests to prevent recurrence.
- Postmortem and an action item to include dedicated-tier smoke tests in every policy rollout.

I’ll continue to monitor — attaching request ids that matched the regression (clear8_request_ids.txt).

M
Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Two asks from Clear8:
1) Please share the timeline for the permanent fix and the postmortem.
2) We’ll need a commercial remediation (credits) for the window of degraded service — Samir, can you share the internal numbers? We can provide request counts if helpful.

Appreciate the rapid response.

-Jill

Date: 2026-11-19T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident update & next steps — Clear8Health safety valve regression

Jill / team —

Follow-up after monitoring overnight and the engineering fixes:
- Root cause: unit conversion bug in the global policy rollout that incorrectly applied minute-window clamping to token/sec calculations for dedicated tenants.
- Resolution: hotfix removed the clamp and full patch with unit test coverage deployed at 16:20 PST 2026-11-19.
- Impact: customer error rate returned to baseline; no further production regressions observed.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-20):
1) Joint postmortem doc with timeline, remediation steps, and action owners (drive link above).
2) Formal remediation offer (credits) — Lauren will propose terms and I’ll route approval.
3) Policy rollout checklist update and a new smoke test that exercises dedicated-tier paths under synthetic bursts.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll share the postmortem and schedule the follow-up call.

Best —
Sofia
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
